To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) stated preferences are time-invariant, and (2) the value of environmental benefits is independent of their timing.
stated preferences are sensitive to the time at which benefits occur, but only for the short-term.

(a) stated preferences are time-insensitive, (b) this time-insensitivity is due to sustainability issues and (c) the time-insensitivity is not affected by the level of information provided to participants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether individuals care about sustainability.

the social desirabilities of environmental interventions that are aimed at counteracting time persistent environmental problems, whose impact occurs over a long period of time, involving the current generation, as well as future generations.
the social desirabilty of environmental projects and policies which produce benefits which will be experienced in the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results are consistent with the idea that the social desirabilities of interventions aiming at the preservation and adaptation to climate change are not time sensitive.
, at least in the case of environmental issues, the time sensitivity of preferences is not a significant concern.

, in the case of climate change and other environmental issues, the value of benefits may be insensitive to the timing of the benefits, but this is only the case because of the nature of the problem itself, and not necessarily because of the way in which individuals value benefits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
individuals do not seem to care about sustainability.
individuals are not time sensitive in their preferences for preservation policies.
individuals are willing to accept the costs of a project to preserve the environment even if it will benefit only the next generation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of time-persistent environmental issues, individuals do not seem to value benefits in terms of their timing, but rather in terms of the sustainability of their outcomes.
the time sensitivity of preferences is not a necessary condition for sustainability, and that sustainability issues can be addressed even when preferences are time insensitive.
, if the social value of environmental benefits is time insensitive, the time horizon of the decision-making process should be extended to include the very long-term.
